questions.history: Remove x once from the two distinct keys.
questions.prediction: On the parent expect the first mapping to disappear before the extra second-view attempt, which may throw UnsupportedOperationException. On the merge expect true, first empty, second still {b=x}, and m.keySet() equal to {b}.
questions.basis: The two visible keys supply two equal occurrences. Collection.remove removes one, and the first view is visited first.
questions.refutation: The merged call throws, returns false, deletes both entries, or leaves the first key instead of the second.

questions.history: Use first {a=x}, second {b=y}. Remove a value absent from both, then remove x.
questions.prediction: On both revisions the results should be false then true. The first call preserves both maps and the second leaves only b=y visible.
questions.basis: Both operations can be decided without deleting any second-map entry.
questions.refutation: A missing value reports success, the unrelated y disappears, or a still maps to x.

questions.history: Hold the first map {a=x} fixed. Give the second the same key a with the distinct value hidden. Capture m.values() before removing x.
questions.prediction: On the merge, a now resolves to hidden through m.get("a"). The captured view contains hidden, excludes x and has size one. The first map is empty and the second still owns a.
questions.basis: The factory documents first-map precedence on colliding keys. Deleting the winning mapping re-exposes the shadowed value through the same view.
questions.refutation: The return flag is true but the captured values stay empty, both maps lose a, or get still returns x.

questions.history: After the merged first removal, call values.remove("x") again while only b=x remains.
questions.prediction: The list regression predicts true followed by an empty collection. At the map boundary a competing source prediction is UnsupportedOperationException with b=x intact. Record the outcome and both maps.
questions.basis: The values view of the filtered second map comes from AbstractMap. Its entry view is a FilteredSet and the Spring FilteredIterator has no remove override. Removal through an iterator is optional.
questions.refutation: An exception with b intact disproves successful single removal on the second call. A true result with an empty second map disproves the iterator-limitation prediction. A false result with b visible satisfies neither.
